title: Device UX · round 1
intro: Claude Design, 19 Nov. Companion on iPhone 18 Pro and iPad Pro 11", light. Three directions for how chrome gives the space back, each on the same six frames: wiki page, session with a permission, the same session reading back, two questions, iPad wiki (landscape) and iPad session (portrait), plus the iPad column states. One navigation model is shared by all three.

A · Fold into the bar (designer's pick): the system's own bars give the space back as you scroll. Headers fold into the bar, request cards fold to a 56-pt row, iPad columns step down with the sidebar button (all · list + detail · detail). Wiki chrome 28% → 13%; transcript under a permission 35% → 47%. Low cost, standard SwiftUI, iPhone Duo bars keep working.

B · Get out of the way: scroll and the bars, banner and mic leave the text; one tap brings them back. A waiting request becomes an amber pill. Wiki chrome 7%, reading back through a transcript 82%, iPad reading view on ⌃⌘F. Medium cost.

C · Everything at the bottom: one bottom bar holds back, title and actions, so the top is all content; on iPad the Macs column becomes a 64-pt rail. Not a system bar (needs its own Duo layout) and on a question the bottom takes 51%. High cost; the designer would leave it out.

Shared navigation: a link to another section (session → #4) pushes on the stack you are in with a back chip naming the origin; ••• › Show in Backlog moves you there for good. Wiki and doc links open in place, never in a popup (the phone stops catching openDoc; the wiki plugin already maps the path to its page). Each segment keeps its own stack and scroll. On iPad the list column shows the section's own tree. Needs you → answer → back 5 → 3 taps; session → #4 → back 1 + 3 → 1 + 1 (iPad: no way back → 1 + 1); wiki → linked page → back: popup → 1 + 1; two questions 5 → 3.

Recommendation: build A, add B's reading mode for wiki pages and docs only plus the iPad reading view; sessions keep A's folded row. Open for the pick: Wiki as its own iPhone segment (Agents · Backlog · Docs · Wiki · More, wiki in 2 taps; shown on A1 only) or under More as today (3 taps).
